title: Candidate ranking and rollback guidelines - Feb 2026
content:
Context and goal:
This doc synthesizes the last two candidate evaluation runs (run-2026-02-08 and run-2026-02-14) for the conversational QA family and codex-like completion tasks. Objective: produce a single ranked candidate list, surface brittle regressions, and define explicit rollout + rollback thresholds for the first round of production onboarding (hosted API tier -> dedicated pool canary).

Quick summary / recommendation:
- Top ranked model: v3-compact-8q (best balance of cost & tail latency; marginally lower long-form exact-match than v2-medium). Recommend canary rollout to 2% traffic on dedicated pool for 2 weeks with automated QA checks.
- Backup (fast-fallback): v2-medium-16q for low-latency routes (p95 latency spikes).
- Disqualify for production: v3-large-fp16 due to intermittent hallucination regressions on the legal prompt set (see "Hallucination incidents" below).

Evaluation methodology (short):
- Datasets: conversational-qa-v1 (3k prompts), legal-extracts (800 prompts, high-sensitivity), code-gen-small (1.5k prompts).
- Signals collected: exact_match, f1, rouge-l, tokenized-bleu for code, hallucination-rate (manual adjudication on flagged differences), semantic-similarity (embedding-based), latency p50/p95, memory OOM incidents, cost-per-1k-tokens(provisioned), and rerate-quality (0-5 human score on 300 sampled responses).
- Match rules: a candidate "wins" vs baseline if it improves primary metric (exact_match for conv-qa, BLEU for code) and does not degrade any secondary safety metric by >2% absolute.
- Aggregation: compute per-dataset normalized z-scores across metrics, then weighted sum (weights: primary 0.5, safety 0.2, latency/cost 0.2, human-quality 0.1).

Leaderboard (top 6 by aggregate score) - condensed view:
1) v3-compact-8q: agg_score 0.87 | conv-qa EM +3.1% | p95 latency +8ms | cost -18%
2) v2-medium-16q: agg_score 0.79 | conv-qa EM +2.4% | p95 latency -12ms | cost -6%
3) v3-medium-8q: agg_score 0.65 | conv-qa EM +1.2% | p95 latency +30ms | cost -12%
4) v3-large-fp16: agg_score 0.61 | conv-qa EM +4.0% | hallucination-rate +2.6pp (bad) | cost +45%
5) v1-stable-32q: agg_score 0.49 | conv-qa EM -0.3% | p95 latency +2ms | cost -5%
6) v3-tiny-quant: agg_score 0.37 | conv-qa EM -6.5% | p95 latency -34ms | cost -60%

Win/Loss matrix (pairwise highlights):
- v3-compact-8q vs v2-medium-16q: wins 58% of cases on conv-qa, losses concentrated on long-form synthesis prompts where v2 produces longer but sometimes verbose answers.
- v3-large-fp16 vs v3-compact-8q: wins on raw EM but loses on safety (hallucination incidents) and costs 2.5x.
- v3-tiny-quant vs v1-stable-32q: wins on latency/cost but loses heavily on correctness for legal prompts.

Hallucination incidents (manual spot-check):
- v3-large-fp16 produced 21 flagged hallucinations across 800 legal prompts (2.6% rate). Examples include invented statute citations and non-existent case law. Root cause hypothesis: mixed-precision kernel mismatch + aggressive context truncation for legal prompts with long doc references.
- v3-compact-8q had 3 flagged incidents (0.4%) on the same set; review of prompts shows prefix tokenization boundary issues.

Performance & reliability notes:
- p95 latency baseline (v1-stable-32q) = 220ms; v3-compact-8q p95=228ms; v2-medium-16q p95=195ms. CPU usage on host nodes increased ~6% for v3 models due to additional kernel overhead.
- Memory: v3-large-fp16 experienced 2 OOM incidents during stress test at global batch size 32; flagged for further infra tuning if we wanted to pursue.

Decision rules for canary rollout (proposed):
1) Canary size: start at 1% for 24h, increase to 2% for 13 days if automated gates pass, then 5% for 3 days before wide rollout.
2) Automated gates each day must show: no increase >0.5pp in hallucination-rate on production prompt monitors, token-error-rate <0.1%, latency p95 within 20% of baseline for the route, and cost-per-1k within expected bounds.
3) Human-in-the-loop: daily sample of 200 responses reviewed by solutions QA during the 2% period; any single-day drop below 4.0 average human-quality rating triggers immediate rollback.
4) Hard rollback thresholds: any single-week cumulative increase >1pp in safety incidents or >30% p95 latency regression => immediate rollback.

Rollback playbook (operational steps):
- Step 0: Circuit-breaker alert triggers SRE and oncall applied-ml.
- Step 1: Quarantine canary traffic and route traffic to fallback candidate (v2-medium-16q) via routing policy redirection (route-id: conv-qa-dedicated-canary).
- Step 2: Snapshot failing request ids, gather tokens, traces, and attach to MLONB-412 ticket.
- Step 3: If incident matches previously seen failure class, escalate to model-owner; if new, create postmortem and hold further rollout.

Open questions / items for next week:
- Should we invest infra cycles to stabilize v3-large-fp16 (fix mixed-precision kernel) or deprioritize due to cost curve? (action: schedule a 2hr deep-dive with infra + applied-ml, owner: Michael Chen)
- Add extra legal prompt augmentations to the automated hallucination detector (owner: Sofia Ramirez).
- Run a 48h extended stress run at batch sizes 16/32 to reproduce OOM and p95 tail behavior (owner: SRE).

Appendix A: sample prompts that flip winners (short list)
- conv-qa-long-context-367: requires preserving citation context across multi-turn -> v2-medium wins
- legal-extract-129: extraction of clause -> v3-compact returns shorter but accurate extraction; v3-large invents clause name
- code-gen-agg-042: multi-file snippet -> v3-medium returns more consistent variable naming

Appendix B: raw metric snapshot references
- run-2026-02-08: s3://redwood-evals/applied-ml/run-2026-02-08/summary.csv
- run-2026-02-14: s3://redwood-evals/applied-ml/run-2026-02-14/summary.csv

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is a a more conservative recommendation than the Feb 8 internal pre-read; we tightened rollback thresholds after the legal set flagged risk.
- If you want a heatmap visualization or the full pairwise matrix, see linked GH evals run (github:repo/redwood/evals#254) or ping me and I’ll drop the notebook.

Next steps (timeline):
- Feb 21: finalize canary config and infra knobs with SRE.
- Feb 22: prepare routing policy and canary job.
- Feb 23: launch 24h 1% canary (if no objections by EOD Feb 21).

Approval (for reviewers): please add a short comment with APPROVE/REJECT and one-line rationale in the doc comments.

-- Aisha K.
